A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HPLT v2 research. Their complete main texts, appendices, tables, and figures support comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original corpus analyses, manual quality annotations, and experiments training masked language models, generative language models, and translation systems.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and reports additional translation results, Chinese quality annotations, and corpus statistics.

M1.justification: V3 adds document-constrained pivoting for DocHPLT: additional bitexts connect sentences through the same aligned English document (Section 3.2). V1 already collected document-alignment outputs and described sentence-pivoted MultiHPLT. The core extraction, cleaning, and model architectures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Reported MT evaluation coverage expands from 35 directions out of English and 34 into English to 50 and 48 respectively (v1 Tables 13-14; v3 Tables 14-15). Additions include Belarusian, Finnish, Lithuanian, Nepali, Tamil, and Xhosa. Manual inspection also expands from 21 to 22 languages by adding Chinese. The MLM and English/Norwegian LM task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The comparator families remain unchanged across MLM, generative-LM, and MT experiments. Tatoeba is relabeled Tatoeba (OPUS) or OPUS rather than replaced. FineWeb-2 was already the Norwegian comparator in v1 Appendix I.2; extending existing comparisons to additional languages does not introduce new baseline methods.

E3.justification: Figure 4 changes the English LM aggregate from average score to average normalized score; Norwegian already used normalized scores. This is a limited evaluation-metric change. Model sizes, token budgets, benchmark splits, and per-language manual sampling procedures remain unchanged, with no evidence establishing training reruns.

E4.justification: V3 Figures 9-10 add language-specific n-grams, translations, and occurrence counts supporting Appendix E's existing discussion of boilerplate, religious content, and other quality indicators. The manual crawl-quality analysis adds Chinese results in Table 12 and Figure 11. Existing cleaning comparisons and crawl-yield analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals for manual quality estimates and corresponding plot error bars. Chinese uses the existing reporting practice. There are no added repeated-run counts, seeds, significance procedures, or model-performance uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V3 adds numerous MT results, Chinese audit statistics, n-gram occurrence counts, and DocHPLT statistics. Its MT summary replaces mixture BLEU scores of 31.64/25.16 into/from English in v1 Figure 6 with 30.5/24.2 in Table 3, alongside COMET averages. Expanded coverage and revised aggregation prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance declines. Existing MLM scores and final-checkpoint LM plots are retained.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. Existing mathematical criteria and algorithm descriptions are retained. The changed English aggregate metric is not accompanied by a new formal definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The document-aligned corpus changes from a planned release in v1's conclusion to the delivered DocHPLT contribution in v3 Section 3.2; future work now concerns further experiments with it. The central claims about 193 languages, approximately 8T tokens, 380M sentence pairs, and downstream usefulness remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The MT discussion drops v1's claim of improvements across all into-English models and presents aggregate advantages instead. V3 also explains why the register taxonomy suits web text. Existing limitations concerning language imbalance, contamination, residual boilerplate, machine-generated content, and punctuation errors remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds direct access information for the HPLT release, OPUS-hosted parallel resources, DocHPLT, MultiHPLT, and the modified OpenLID model. It also explicitly documents common-direction averaging for MT comparisons. Most implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, and compute budgets were already present in v1.

R1.justification: V3 adds the NorEval paper and expands Section 2's explicit comparison with the predecessor HPLT v1.2 release. Collapsing duplicate Conneau references and updating the Norwegian QA paper's publication information concern existing works rather than additional research.

P1.justification: Targeted revisions include an expanded predecessor comparison, DocHPLT paragraphs, a rewritten and reordered MT section, revised conclusion, and added acknowledgements and affiliation information. Most prose and the overall section and Appendix A-K structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 replaces the MT bar chart with a two-part BLEU/COMET table, expands and reorders the MT appendix tables, adds two extensive n-gram figures, and redraws the English LM plot with new axes and markers. It also relocates the manual-audit and final-checkpoint plots to the document's end, substantially changing visual organization.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens the paper through broader reported MT coverage, Chinese quality inspection, concrete evidence for content-quality observations, and clearer resource access and predecessor comparisons. Its MT summary also makes comparison scope explicit. These are useful incremental gains, although reporting inconsistencies remain: the into-English averages in Table 3 do not reproduce from the common-direction rows in Table 15.
